label: Someone pays for governance (not free/expected)
kill_criterion: If MSPs treat agent governance as a hygiene expectation owed for free by whoever created the agent, no standalone revenue attaches to the governance capability.
test_that_resolves_it: Pricing conversation with 5 MSPs: 'would you pay a distinct line item for agent governance, or expect it bundled with the tool that runs the agent?'
evidence: [A] Shawn (advises 200+ MSPs): governance is 'probably not something you're going to get someone to pay for' [CS: HIGH-against, offerings:62]. The offering already concedes governance is NOT a SKU (offerings:171).

label: Agent-management seat ARPU exists at a defensible price
kill_criterion: If no price point holds for an agent-management seat (buyer anchors to per-tech RMM pricing or to zero), the seat pillar of monetization has no floor.
test_that_resolves_it: Same 5-MSP pricing conversation; probe a number for a per-tech agent-management seat and compare to Atera $129-219/tech/mo RMM anchor.
evidence: [?] Agent-seat ARPU has NO price precedent, tagged 'MOST FRAGILE' [CS: UNKNOWN, tam-control-plane:57]. Only per-tech benchmark is single-vendor Atera [WOBBLY].

label: Can govern externally-built agents (the moat)
kill_criterion: If ACP can only audit externally-built agents after the fact (no pre-screen, no intercept-and-gate), it does not govern them, and the 'control plane' framing is false for anything the MSP didn't build in ACP.
test_that_resolves_it: G4 Action Proxy spec run: can the proxy technically intercept+gate a third-party agent's actions? Plus 3 operator interviews: 'would you route your Cloud/Claude-built agents through our gate, and why?'
evidence: [?] Nicole's own BIG QUESTION; today 'audit-after, no pre-screen... not specced' [CS: VERIFIED, why-nable-build-map:66]. Vision doc: 'does not pre-screen or approve runbooks before use... a big unknown.'

label: Gated autonomy is wanted
kill_criterion: If MSPs do NOT want gated autonomy (want either full autonomy or none), the risk-tier model is over-engineered. No evidence supports this; strong evidence against.
test_that_resolves_it: Already answered. Any further test would be confirmatory only.
evidence: [R] 5/5 transcripts + 13/17 Condens + all-17-expect-human-control [CS: HIGH, offerings:57]. 'Governance + rollback = price of entry' [blind-interviews:55]. NOTE: strong need = table stakes (Kano risk), not premium.

label: Governance-as-bill-enablement works (MSPs pay for the ability to charge their clients)
kill_criterion: If the 'charge my clients' motive is idiosyncratic to one buyer and doesn't generalize, the reframe from cost-to-revenue-enabler collapses.
test_that_resolves_it: In the 5-MSP pricing conversation, probe whether governance is valued as a client-billing enabler independent of the person who raised it.
evidence: [A] Jonathan, unprompted: buys control plane for 'the ability to charge on a monthly basis... a recurring revenue generator' [CS: MEDIUM, offerings:60]. Single source.

label: Determinism demand aligns with the Deterministic Substitution Engine
kill_criterion: If customers want AI that reasons freely rather than locked deterministic workflows, the DSE alignment narrows the product's positioning instead of strengthening it.
test_that_resolves_it: Probe Shawn/Vikram-type buyers on whether they want locked-deterministic or free-reasoning agents, and for which job types.
evidence: [A]/MEDIUM Shawn + Vikram want 'locked deterministic' workflows (offerings:65). Also flagged as possibly narrowing 'AI Coworker that reasons freely' positioning (offerings:74).

label: MSPs want to build their own agents (build-your-own = retention)
kill_criterion: If MSPs only want pre-spec'd agents and never build their own, the retention thesis (build-your-own keeps them) fails and B is just a pre-built catalog.
test_that_resolves_it: Track, in a pilot, whether MSPs progress from pre-spec'd coworkers to authoring their own; measure the ratio.
evidence: [A] Pre-spec'd on-ramp / build-your-own retention split (offerings:169). Assumption, not tested.

label: Per-run metering does not trigger bill-shock
kill_criterion: If usage-coupled per-run billing produces unpredictable bills that scale with the MSP's success, bill-shock drives exactly the self-build the model was meant to prevent.
test_that_resolves_it: Model a 200-agent MSP's monthly run volume at candidate per-run prices; test the bill against MSP tolerance in interview.
evidence: [A] Bill-shock is named as 'the fear that drives self-build' (prompt). Per-run metering unpriced [tam-control-plane:58].

label: EU AI Act makes the audit trail a compliance asset (net tailwind)
kill_criterion: If mandatory logging commoditizes audit trails (every runtime must ship it to be sellable), the regulation is a commoditizing force, not a differentiator; and if the schema is only accidentally compliant, it is a liability not an asset.
test_that_resolves_it: Assigned compliance owner (currently <TBD>) verifies schema against actual EU AI Act requirements; assess whether logging is differentiator or table-stakes.
evidence: [CS: LOW - outside model training window, do not assert as fact]. Schema is 'only accidentally AI-Act-shaped'; compliance owner <TBD> (offerings:182).

label: Governing an agent does not increase N-able's liability
kill_criterion: If assuming a governance role (approve/log/permit) establishes a duty of care, then a governed-agent error makes N-able's audit trail a discovery document that indicts rather than protects.
test_that_resolves_it: Legal review: does operating a governance-of-record plane create duty-of-care / product-liability exposure when a governed action still errs? Route to compliance owner.
evidence: [?] Derek: 'AIs cannot be taken to court... there has to be a human in the loop' [CS: HIGH]. Batch approval default 'Approve all' (findings JSON) reads as rubber-stamp in litigation. Unexamined.

label: Governor-of-all-agents is technically and commercially viable
kill_criterion: If externally-built agents won't voluntarily route through ACP, or ACP can't safely be trusted with intercept/block scope across everyone's critical path, the governor-of-all-agents moat cannot exist and B is a walled garden with no moat.
test_that_resolves_it: G4 Action Proxy architecture spike (can it intercept-and-gate) + operator willingness interviews (would they route third-party agents through it). Same test as B3 from the strategy side.
evidence: [?] The moat and the deepest hole are the same fact. Action Proxy 'must sit in the action path (latency, adoption)' [word-sketches:104]. Walled-garden vs governor 'load-bearing decision' unmade (offerings:172).

label: Metering the MSP's own / cross-tenant agent runs is legal and desirable
kill_criterion: If per-run metering bills for actions executed inside a third party's (the MSP's client's) environment without that client's consent, it is a DPA/consent problem, not just a pricing choice.
test_that_resolves_it: Legal/contract review of metering actions that touch client-owned infrastructure; MSP interview on whether metering their own agents is acceptable.
evidence: [?] Unexamined. Runs execute against the MSP's clients' infrastructure under the client's contract; metering cross-tenant actions has no consent scoping surfaced.

label: B is not confused with / cannibalized by N-central's existing automation
kill_criterion: If MSPs already inside N-central see governed automation as 'what my RMM policies already do', B faces channel/positioning confusion and its honest value narrows to the AI-reasoning wrapper.
test_that_resolves_it: Position-test B against N-central automation with existing N-central MSPs: 'why is this a separate product from your RMM policies?'
evidence: [A] N-central already runs rule-based automation: patch via group policy, service control, scripted remediation [CS: VERIFIED, 06-ncentral-automation-patterns.md]. Internal substitute unmodeled.

label: Action-proxy latency is acceptable in the critical path
kill_criterion: If routing every governed action through ACP's gate (itself calling external LLMs) adds latency that degrades time-sensitive automation (threat response, alert-flood suppression), the proxy tax makes B unusable for the highest-value jobs.
test_that_resolves_it: Benchmark added latency of an action routed through the proxy vs direct; set an SLA; test against the fastest-cadence use case.
evidence: [?] Risk named — 'you must sit in the action path (latency, adoption)' [word-sketches:104] — but never measured. No latency budget, SLA, or benchmark exists.

label: The operator can safely configure a governed agent
kill_criterion: If a non-programmer MSP admin cannot hold the mental model of risk tiers + batch approvals + promotion criteria + scope guardrails, they misconfigure the safety, and the governance is theater.
test_that_resolves_it: Watch 3-5 real MSP admins configure the 9-field Coworker Brief cold; measure misconfiguration of the risk ceiling and scope.
evidence: [A] The operator/daily user was never studied; ~93% [A] on the daily user (vision-synthesis). B's safety depends on correct configuration by an unstudied operator.

label: The autonomy-promotion criterion is definable safely
kill_criterion: Too-liberal criterion promotes an untrustworthy agent to auto-execute ('one miss kills the relationship'); too-conservative criterion never delivers the autonomy payoff that justifies the seat. Undefined = both risks live.
test_that_resolves_it: Design spike defining the evidence standard for Manual->Assisted->Autonomous; risk-tolerance call routed to Beth/Meaghan/Nicole.
evidence: [?] Approval model 'does not decide when to promote'; separate system governs it, criterion undefined [findings JSON; council-mini-alert-flood]. Safety-critical, unspecced.

label: Drift detection for locked deterministic runbooks is solvable
kill_criterion: A locked runbook that keeps executing after the environment drifts (patched OS, changed API, renamed field) confidently does the wrong thing at scale - worse than no automation.
test_that_resolves_it: Spec the drift-detection + unfreeze mechanic ('lock it once it works, until something goes wrong'); test against a deliberately drifted environment.
evidence: [?] Determinism is B's best superpower-alignment but the drift-detection mechanic is unspecced (offerings:170). Silent + scaled failure mode.

label: The Expert/Vendor marketplace supply side ignites
kill_criterion: A two-sided marketplace with no committed vendor supply and [A]-only demand fails to reach critical mass (classic cold-start); any TAM ceiling leaning on rev-share collapses to the floor.
test_that_resolves_it: Secure named committed vendor-Expert supply commitments before counting marketplace rev-share in TAM.
evidence: [A] Marketplace ranked last, 6/6, demand [A] (offerings:167); 'needs supply side first... heavy + slow' [word-sketches:113]. No vendor partners named as committed.

label: Per-run metering is priceable at all
kill_criterion: If no legitimate per-run price can be derived (no benchmark for metering governed autonomous infrastructure actions), per-run metering is not a viable revenue pillar, not just an unset number.
test_that_resolves_it: Attempt to derive a defensible per-run price from a real cost model + willingness test; if none holds, drop the pillar.
evidence: [?] 'EXCLUDED. No public benchmark. [CS: FABRICATION RISK if numeric]... unquantifiable from public data' [tam-control-plane:58,80]. n8n/Zapier meter integration steps, not governed infra actions - wrong analog.

label: The versioned/guardrail governance registry actually gets built
kill_criterion: Without a versioned registry, B cannot answer 'what was this agent permitted to do on the date it erred' - the core audit and liability question. The 'lowest build risk' boast is true for the engine, false for the registry.
test_that_resolves_it: Migrate the designed versioned/guardrail registry from flat pre-registry tables; verify it answers the point-in-time-permission audit query.
evidence: [A]/[?] Coworker/Expert are 'flat pre-registry tables (versioned/guardrail registry designed, not migrated)' [why-nable-build-map:65]. Build-state gap hidden inside a build-readiness boast.

label: B survives as a standalone offering (not merely the seat under A/C)
kill_criterion: If standalone governance WTP is ~zero (B1 fails), B is not an offering - it is the priced seat/infrastructure under A and C. Fatal to B-as-a-standalone-bet, though not to N-able.
test_that_resolves_it: Resolve B1 + B2. If standalone WTP is zero, reposition B as the seat under A/C rather than a standalone offering with its own TAM.
evidence: [?] The offering itself half-concedes this: governance 'NOT a SKU' (offerings:171); price B 'as the seat under A/C' (offerings:164). Treating B as a standalone $3B-TAM product may be the category error.
